notes:
82 place entries from the three texts. I read all three in full and did not modify any project file.

How I tested: every pattern was compiled as (?<!\w)(?:pattern) and run over every text unit of the three texts. The units were Zacher c<n>/n<n> (latin, ru, en and the note source field), Odyssey s1–s4 and n1a…n4a (grc, ru, en), and article abstract, s1–s6, n1–n38 and appx-1…12. With all languages' patterns applied to all fields, no pattern hit a word in another script by mistake. Units per entity: Laestrygonia 13; Sicily 9; Egypt 8; Libya, Alexandria and Aeolia 6 each; Macedonia, Thebes and Italy 5 each; most of the rest 1–4.

Scanner advice: several units name a place only in embedded Greek or Latin. Examples: article n35 (Τηλέπυλον), n26 (ἐν τῇ ἔσω θαλάσσῃ / ἐν τῇ ἔξω), n31 (τῶν ἀνέμων νῆσον) and n14 (Λαιστρυγόνας). If patterns are applied only by field language, those hits are lost: Telepylos, Mediterranean, Ocean, Aeolia and Laestrygonia each drop by one unit. Apply grc and la patterns to all text. Exclude regexes are meant to match at the start position of the false hit. They cover Rome in Zacher n3 ("whom the Romans call explorator") and Lamos against "Lamomentea" in n24.

What the patterns match:
- Each toponym in all its case forms. Latin patterns allow -que/-ve/-ne (Asiamque, Taurumque).
- Ethnic names only where they stand for a city's citizens or for a place known only through its people. These are Tyrians, Thebans, Corinthians, Athenians, Romans, Acarnanians ("rex Acernanum"), Leontines, Camarinaeans, Acragantines, and the mythical Laestrygonians, Cimmerians (including Crates' variant Κερβέριοι), Lotus-eaters and Cyclopes.
- Origin epithets: Малльский, Родосский, Гераклейский, Фиванский, Милетский, дельфийский, олимпийский, истмийский.
- Country-level ethnics and adjectives are deliberately not matched, because they mostly mean the army or the language. These are египетский / Aegyptii / Egyptian, македоняне / Macedones, греческий and персы. As a result Zacher c1 is a hit for Egypt only through the English "Egypt".

Deliberately left out:
- Peoples with no place name in the texts: the Persians (there is no "Persia"), and the c2 list of Indians, Arabs, Phoenicians, Parthians, Assyrians, Scythians, Alans, Oxydracae, Seres, Caucones, Iberians, Agriophagi and Euonymitae.
- "Oriens / Восток" (c2, c8).
- Unnamed features: the strait (πορθμός, Σ 10.1, i.e. Messina) and the river in n62.
- Place names that only identify manuscripts or editions. These are the Turin palimpsest, the Paris, Milan/Ambrosian, Marcianus, Hamburg, Palatine-Heidelberg and Moscow codices, the Aldine, "Rom." (the Rome edition of Eustathius), Oxford, and "Venice 1842" in the n24 source.
- Vincent of Beauvais (n32).
- The bibliography.

ID choices to check:
- Greece is Q41, the modern country. Q11772 (Ancient Greece) is described as a civilisation, not a place.
- Macedonia is Q83958 (the ancient kingdom), paired with Pleiades 491656 (the region).
- Achaea is the Roman province (Q204772 / Pleiades 981502), because for Valerius "Achaia" means Greece.
- Elis is the region (570221), not the city (570220).
- Lycaonia uses Pleiades 648698 (region). 1001911 is the Late Roman province.
- Asia has no Pleiades ID: 915832 is an unlocated label on a Barrington map, not the continent.
- The temple entry is Q11056 "Temple of Ptah", whose coordinates fall at Memphis/Mit Rahina. Pleiades has no record for it; Per-Ptah 795843 is in Nubia.
- Ocean is Q107549003 and Pleiades 608104479 ("River Oceanus"). I gave it kind "sea" because Crates treats it as a real outer ocean; you may prefer "mythical".
- The four "land of …" entries carry the Wikidata item for the people (Laestrygonians Q743931, Cimmerians Q1108676, Lotus-eaters Q596552, cyclops Q128430). Pleiades has none. Its 462275 "Laestrygonii Campi" is the real plain in Sicily and its 135663336 "Kimmerioi" is the historical people, so I did not use either.

Left blank on purpose:
- Lamos: the only Wikidata item is Q16328054, king Lamus.
- Telmessus: Aristander's home could be the Lycian city (Q1145385 / Pleiades 639137) or the Carian one (Q1642438 / 599959).
- Hicesia: Pleiades 452336 gives it, but it identifies the island with Basiluzzo (Q810177), and the Odyssey note says the identification is disputed (Panarea Q654105 is the other candidate). So I gave the Pleiades ID only.

Every Wikidata ID was confirmed with wbgetentities (label and description) and every Pleiades ID through /places/<id>/json (title). Candidates were found with wbsearchentities, with the Wikidata SPARQL endpoint used as an extra lookup because the API was rate-limiting.
